pr_title: sql: scan the system.role_members table using a single scan
pr_body:
relates to support case https://github.com/cockroachlabs/support/issues/1463
fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/77452

### sql: use singleflight for role membership lookups

This helps prevent a thundering herd when this cache gets invalidated.

### sql: scan the system.role_members table using a single scan


Release note (sql change): Added a
`sql.auth.resolve_membership_single_scan.enabled` cluster setting, which
changes the query for an internal role membership cache. Previously the
code would recursively look up each role in the membership hierarchy,
leading to multiple queries. With the setting on, it uses a single
query. The setting is true by default.

### sql: fix information_schema role introspection

Release note (bug fix): The information_schema tables
administrable_role_authorizations and applicable_roles were incorrectly
always returning the current user for the grantee column. Now, the
column will contain the correct role that was granted the parent role
given in the role_name column.

Release justification: high priority bug fix
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/77359)
yeah, i was planning to backport, but change the cluster setting to default to false in 21.2

@rafiss can you try out this query on your data:

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE cte_members (role, path, admin, cycle) AS (
                         SELECT role, ARRAY[$1], "isAdmin", false
                           FROM system.role_members
                          WHERE member = $1
                         UNION ALL SELECT parent.role,
                                          child.path || parent.member,
                                          parent."isAdmin",
                                          parent.member = ANY (child.path)
                                     FROM system.role_members AS parent
                               INNER JOIN cte_members AS child ON parent.member
                                                                  = child.role
                                                              AND NOT cycle
                     )
        SELECT $1, role, bool_or(admin) AS "isAdmin" -- note we don't need to return the member back
          FROM cte_members
      GROUP BY role;
```
That query also is taking a long time (it's been running more than 1 minute).
should we just use a single SQL scan then?

> should we just use a single SQL scan then?

yep, done
I changed the default value of `sql.auth.resolve_membership_single_scan.enabled` to be a metamorphic constant, so test builds have a chance of defaulting to false.

issue_context.title: sql: Improve role membership cold cache scenarios
issue_context.body:
This issue tracks two problems:

In order to check privileges for SQL commands, we must check not just the privilege for the current user, but also all parent (and grandparent, etc) roles for that user.

Normally, the role membership information is cached, so checking privileges is quick. However, this cache of memberships needs to be cleared whenever users are modified.

We have received reports of slowness (~10 seconds) coming from the time it takes to rebuild the cache. Rebuilding the cache can happen WHILE executing almost any command, since it happens while checking if the user has privileges to run the command.

We've found two problems:

1. We have some inefficient logic that means we run multiple internal queries to construct the role membership tree. Specifically, we do one query for each layer of the role membership hierarchy. This is bad because each of these queries can result in a network hop to another node in the cluster. we can change this so it happens all in one query. See https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6880665c589c6a49e3f985ed2cc3448052d26763/pkg/sql/authorization.go#L467-L516
2. Another problem is that if there are multiple user-initiated queries happening at the same time, then it’s possible for each one of them to try to repopulate the cache. This means each one of them will kick off multiple internal queries, causing more overhead in the cluster. We can fix this so that there’s only one “cache reconstruction” happening at a time. See https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6880665c589c6a49e3f985ed2cc3448052d26763/pkg/sql/authorization.go#L430-L433

This issue tracks improving those cases. We currently are planning to create a backport for problem 1, but not problem 2.

Jira issue: CRDB-13599
Epic CRDB-8948
comments:
> We currently are planning to create a backport for problem 1, but not problem 2.

I support backporting both of these fixes.
I'd argue that the fact that ongoing transactions incur an extra round-trip at all is surprising and worthy of an issue in its own right.

> I support backporting both of these fixes.

OK - the singleflight change turned out to be pretty small so I'll go ahead and backport that too.
